  degree-genus divisor, prove its openness/base-change behavior, and expose the exact

  outside this write set is needed, request it through the coordination conversation
  rather than editing that file. Require narrow kernel checks, standard axiom audits,
  an immediate consumer theorem, and normal proof budgets. Do not resume the high-degree
  Abel quotient route.'

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once.       "body": "SESSION-END RE-MEASUREMENT (review-ajcr r6 close). The count moved AGAIN during one session: 23 -> 1 -> 23. Do not quote a number from this item; run the command.\n\nNOW, shared index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` + `--shortstat`:\n  33 files changed, 96 insertions(+), 1229 DELETIONS(-)  -- 23 staged D\nALL 23 verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk, so nothing is lost as of this writing. They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

35	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    36	
    37	noncomputable section
    38	
    39	/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    40	def divRankOneUniversalPredicate :
    41	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    42	  divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi
    43	
    44	/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.
    45	
    46	Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
    47	Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
    48	def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    49	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
    50	  Subfunctor.range (yoneda.map
    51	    (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι))
    52	
    53	/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.
    54	
    55	The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
    56	preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
    57	is manufactured here. -/
    58	structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
    59	  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
    60	  carrier_eq :
    61	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
    62	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi
    63	
    64	/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
    65	def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
    66	  h.carrier.toScheme
    67	
    68	/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
    69	def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    70	    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
    71	  h.carrier.ι
    72	
    73	theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
    74	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    75	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
    76	  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
    77	  infer_instance
    78	
    79	/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
    80	divisor functor. -/
    81	def divRankOneOpenOver (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    82	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    83	  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
    84	
    85	/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
    86	def divRankOneOpenPullback
    87	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    88	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
    89	  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier
    90	
    91	theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
    92	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    93	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    94	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
    95	  infer_instance
    96	
    97	/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
    98	theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
    99	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   100	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
   101	    (x : T.left) :
   102	    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
   103	  rfl
   104	
   105	/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
   106	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
   107	    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
   108	  rfl
   109	
   110	/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
   111	theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
   112	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   113	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
   114	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
   115	  h.carrier_eq
   116	
   117	/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.
   118	
   119	The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
   120	replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
   121	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
   122	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   123	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   124	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   125	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   126	      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
   127	  rw [h.carrier_eq]
   128	
   129	/-- A point in the certified open carrier is a point of the universal rank-one predicate. -/
   130	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_of_carrier
   131	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   132	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   133	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   134	    (hx : x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T) :
   135	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T := by
   136	  exact (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x).mpr hx
   137	
   138	/- The logical rank-one predicate remains stable under arbitrary pullback, independently of the
   139	   geometric witness used to represent it by an open. -/
   140	theorem divRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem
   141	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   142	    (f : T ⟶ T')
   143	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   144	    (hx : x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T) :
   145	    (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).map f x ∈
   146	      (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T' :=
   147	  (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).map f hx
   148	
   149	end

   106	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   107	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   108	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   109	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   110	
   111	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   112	
   113	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   114	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   115	relative-open gate below. -/
   116	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   117	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   118	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   119	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   120	
   121	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   122	
   123	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   124	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   125	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
   126	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   127	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
   128	
   129	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   130	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
   131	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
   132	  h
   133

   135	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   136	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   137	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   138	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   139	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   140	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   141	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
   142	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
   143	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   144	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   145	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   146	  h.property g fst snd hpb
   147	
   148	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   149	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   150	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   151	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   152	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   153	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h
   154	
   155	/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
   156	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   157	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   158	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   159	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   160	  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h
   161	
   162	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
   163	
   164	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
   165	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
   166	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
   167	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
   168	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   169	
   170	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
   171	representer. -/
   172	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
   173	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
   174	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
   175	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   176	
   177	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   178	def rankOneAbelAff :
   179	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
   180	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   181	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   182	
   183	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   184	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
   185	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   186	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
   187	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
   188	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   189	
   190	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   191	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   192	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   193	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   194	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi

   196	/-- Immediate consumer theorem: the restricted represented Abel map lands in the public locus.
   197	The stronger canonical inverse still needs the family-level divisor/evaluation producer; this
   198	theorem records the exact target API that consumer lanes can use today. -/
   199	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}

   201	    ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x :
   202	      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
   203	  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property
